text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli air force hits inside Lebanon
- 30 women prisoners freed
- Banker agrees to cut his own salary
- PM leaves for Washington today
- Court rejects petition against release of six Palestinian women
- Riots over disputed quarry
- Ivry commission's interim findings on crash expected this week
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu to ask Clinton to press Syria to stop protecting Hizbollah
- Security document: 20 Palestinian Authority institutions continue operating in Jerusalem
- Three soldiers killed in bus crash
- Value-education administration recommends 40 centres of Jewish education, ignores Arab sector
- France, India bought from Israel new instrument to prevent plane crashes
MAARIV
- Deep bombardments in Lebanon - a warning signal to Syria
- Warning letter to be sent this week to commander of helicopter fleet over inquiry
- Government will give press videotapes of Netanyahu for news
- Special supplement on soldiers killed in crash
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Threat to Assad: we will not sit still
- Lowest commissions at Bank Hapoalim
- Army challenges court decision to recognise gay partner as army widower
- New regulation requires women seeking abortion to present photograph of fetus from ultrasound
